title: Adding and taking away within 10
summary: Put apples together, take some away and compare. Then make 10 from two numbers.
guide: This studio is for Year 1. Your child works with counters and answers by tapping a number, so no writing is needed. If they can't read yet, read the sentences to them.
A ten-frame has two rows of 5. When counters sit in it, a child can see that 7 is "5 and 2 more" without counting every one.

{{term:addition}} means putting two groups together. {{term:subtraction}} means taking away, or comparing two groups (how many more?). The last mission splits 10 into two parts: these are the number bonds of 10.

engine.instruction-cross: Tap an apple to cross it out.
engine.instruction-ring: Circle the apples with no partner.
engine.instruction-paint: Tap a counter to change its colour.

join.title: How many altogether?
join.prompt: Ali has 3 apples. Sara has 4 apples. Put all the apples in the basket. How many apples are in the basket?
join.hint: Tap each apple to move it to the basket. One row of the basket holds 5. 5 and how many more?
join.success: Well done! 3 apples and 4 apples make 7 apples. 3 + 4 = 7
join.why: If you put the 4 yellow apples in first and then the 3 red ones, do you still get 7? Why?
join.model: Yes. They are the same apples, just in a different order. So 4 + 3 = 7 and 3 + 4 = 7.

feedback.too-many: There are still apples on a plate. Tap them to move them to the basket.
feedback.one-group: That's only the apples from one plate. Count all the apples in the basket.
feedback.took-away: We put the apples together; we didn't take any away. Putting together makes more.
feedback.too-big: That's too many. Count each apple only once.
feedback.too-small: That's too few. Touch each apple as you count it.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

take-away.title: How many are left?
take-away.prompt: Zahra had 8 apples. She ate 3. Cross out 3 apples. How many apples are left?
take-away.hint: Cross out 3 apples. Then count only the apples without a cross.
take-away.why: How can you tell your answer is right? Put the crossed-out apples back and count.
take-away.model: 5 apples are left and 3 were eaten. 5 + 3 = 8. That's the 8 apples we started with, so the answer is right.

feedback.marked-too-many: You crossed out too many. Only 3. Tap an apple again to remove its cross.
feedback.counted-taken: Zahra ate those 3. Count the apples that are left.
feedback.counted-start: There were 8 at the start. Zahra ate 3, so fewer are left now.
feedback.too-big: Count the apples without a cross again.
feedback.too-small: Count the apples without a cross again.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

compare.title: How many more?
compare.prompt: Sara has 7 apples. Reza has 4 apples. Circle Sara's apples that have no partner. How many more apples does Sara have?
compare.hint: Each of Sara's apples pairs with the apple under it. Which ones have an empty space under them?
compare.success: Well done! Sara has 3 more apples. 7 − 4 = 3
compare.why: How many more apples does Reza need to have as many as Sara? Why?
compare.model: 3 apples, because 3 of Sara's apples have no partner. If Reza gets 3 more, they all pair up: 4 + 3 = 7.

feedback.marked-too-few: There's still an apple with no partner. Which of Sara's apples has an empty space under it?
feedback.marked-too-many: You circled an apple that has a partner. Circle only the ones with no partner.
feedback.bigger-row: 7 is all of Sara's apples. We want to know how many more she has.
feedback.smaller-row: 4 is Reza's apples. Count the apples with no partner.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

bond-10.title: Split 10 in two
bond-10.prompt: Here are 10 counters. Keep 6 red. Make the rest yellow. How many are yellow?
bond-10.hint: Tap a counter to make it yellow. One row is 5, so 6 is one row and one more.
bond-10.why: Can you make 10 from two other numbers? Say one and show it.
bond-10.model: Yes. For example 7 and 3, 5 and 5, or 9 and 1. Each time some counters are red and the rest are yellow, and together there are always 10.

feedback.wrong-colors: 6 counters should be red and the rest yellow. Count the red ones.
feedback.same-part: 6 are red. We want the number of yellow counters.
feedback.whole: 10 is all the counters. Count only the yellow ones.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.
